The source text (torah_198.txt) is a single-sentence teaching based on Exodus 14:15 — 'Why do you cry out to Me? Speak to the Children of Israel and let them travel.' The teaching's claim is: when one cries out (צועק) to God, one is told to travel/move (ליסע). This is a pure eitza (cause-and-effect) statement — crying out produces or elicits the instruction to move. The text contains no bechina language whatsoever (no בחינת, no היינו, no נקרא, no הוא בחינת). There are no parallel-nature equivalences being drawn; the only relationship is directional: prayer/crying → action/movement. Without any bechina edges, no connected components can be formed, and therefore no packages can be proposed.
